input.question: If I traveled to space in a space ship that remained completely stationary, would I age faster than those on earth?
input.ground_truth: Due to special relativity, "completely stationary" doesn't make sense. In your reference frame, you would be stationary, so you would age faster. To someone on Earth, the planet would be stationary, so people on Earth would age faster.

response.prediction:
Let’s imagine you and your friend are both playing with toys. You get in a special toy car (the spaceship) that doesn’t move at all—it just stays in one spot. Your friend stays on the ground (on Earth).

Now, according to a big idea called Einstein’s theory of relativity, time can go a little bit differently depending on how fast you are moving and where you are (like if you’re near a big planet like Earth).

But in your case, your spaceship isn’t moving at all compared to Earth. It’s just sitting still. So, time for you and your friend on Earth will go almost exactly the same way. You both will grow up and get older at almost the same speed. 

But if your spaceship was zooming super fast around Earth, or if it was very close to a very heavy thing like a black hole, then time might go a little bit differently for you. But since your spaceship is just sitting still, you both will age about the same!
